text:
maria: Heads-up: noticed a perf regression on long-seq runs after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. p95 latency up ~25% on our 2.1B baseline. nsys traces attached, but wanted to surface here before I dig deeper. Anyone seen this? :thinking_face:

alex: Which commit/PR? any repro command I can run locally?

maria: PR is #1428 (kernel-selector: prefer fused_attn for short heads). Repro command I used: 
```
./run_profiler --model redwood/2.1b --seq 2048 --batch 8 --profile nsys --runs 50
```
Before (commit 8a1f): p95=210ms, After (PR merged): p95=260ms.

jin: Do you have kv-cache hit rates / eviction counters? looks like a KV churn pattern in the trace summary. Perfetto shows a burst of memcpy + kernel launches around token 280-320.

maria: kv stats from the run: 
```
KV hits: 92.1%
KV evictions/sec: 14.8
Memcopy (host->dev) spikes at 280 tokens
```

ben: I'll kick off a bisect job against the range (8a1f..HEAD) with nsys snapshots on each step. If it repros deterministically we should find the commit quickly.

ci-bot: automated-bisect started for range 8a1f..d3e9 (approx 18 commits). First 6 runs scheduled on dedicated-gpu-pool-2. We'll post results here when available. :gear:

sam: Quick thought: the PR also changed the batching heuristic to prefer tighter micro-batching when fused_attn is chosen. Could interact badly with our KV prefetch window and increase memcopies.

jin: I pulled the nsys flame for before/after and overlaid kernel timelines: before used `fused_attn` at 1.2ms, after we see a mix of `fused_attn` + `fwd_attn_split` with lots of small launches (~0.2ms each) and increased host syncs. Looks like more kernel launch overhead + copying. snippet: 
```
nsys report summary:
- before: fused_attn x1 per token, stable launch times
- after: fused_attn x0.6, fwd_attn_split x0.4, hostMemcpy spikes + 30%
```

alex: If kernel selection causes smaller kernels to run more often, that can defeat batching and disable some KV cache reuse. Can you reproduce with `--force-kernel fused_attn`?

maria: Re-ran with forced kernel: p95 goes back to ~212ms. So kernel choice matters. But bisect shows something else: ci-bot posted a hit on commit d1c9b (batcher: early-warmup-exit) as the first failing commit.

ci-bot: bisect result: failing commit: d1c9b5ea (batcher: early-warmup-exit). Attempted reproducer command and nsys capture uploaded to: https://internal-nsys/storage/1755006789-d1c9b.nsys

ben: Interesting — that commit short-circuits micro-batch warming when fused_attn is detected to avoid spending time on warmup for tiny kernels. If warmup skipped, we might be hitting cold paths more often and causing those memcopies.

sam: That meshes with observed launch fragmentation. Warmup prevents small kernels from thrashing the KV prefetch window. Without it, we get lots of tiny kernels and frequent prefix cache misses.

jin: To confirm: I ran the repro with `--warmup-steps=16` forced (overriding early-exit). p95 returned to baseline and memcopy spikes disappeared in perfetto.

maria: Great catch. I'll file a revert PR for d1c9b5ea and open a follow-up that preserves warmup for long-seq workloads while keeping the short-head optimization.

qa-bot: Note: regression only showed up on dedicated-gpu-pool-2 (A100sm) and didn't reproduce on the dev cluster with V100s. Might be hardware/kernel interaction. Marking as high priority for Dedicated customers.

alex: Next actions: 1) revert d1c9b5ea 2) add a unit/integration test that runs a long-seq profile on CI with warmup toggles 3) add an eval that checks KV eviction rate bump as a regression signal.

maria: Will open PRs now and post links. Thanks for the quick triage team. :raised_hands:
